subject.title: fix(doctor): warn when maxActiveTranscriptBytes is set without truncateAfterCompaction

question: Should default `openclaw doctor --lint` treat a positive `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` without `truncateAfterCompaction: true` as a warning that changes the lint result for existing configurations?
rationale: The patch correctly detects a documented no-op setting, but whether the default Doctor contract should newly flag that configuration is a user-facing compatibility and operator-policy choice.

options.title: Keep the default warning
options.body: Merge the check so Doctor lint surfaces an ineffective byte guard and operators can enable truncation or remove the unused setting.

options.title: Make it opt-in advice
options.body: Keep the detection but place it behind an explicitly selected advisory check so existing default lint automation remains unchanged.

recommendation.title: Keep the default warning
recommendation.body: Merge the check so Doctor lint surfaces an ineffective byte guard and operators can enable truncation or remove the unused setting.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available feature-history routing candidate for the transcript-byte-limit behavior.
